paraphrases: Fed kept buying $45bn/month of Treasuries.
Committee maintained QE3 Treasury purchases at $45 billion per month.
FOMC continued asset purchases at $45B monthly in longer-term Treasuries.
decoys: Committee slowed Treasury purchases to $35 billion per month.
Fed announced it would end Treasury purchases entirely at this meeting.

points.point: Committee continued QE3 agency MBS purchases at $40 billion per month
points.quote: continue purchases of MBS at a pace of $40 billion per month and purchases of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $45 billion per month
paraphrases: Fed kept buying $40bn/month of agency MBS.

points.quote: Ms. George dissented because she continued to view monetary policy as overly accommodative and therefore as posing risks
paraphrases: George dissented from the decision.
Esther George voted against the decision.
The sole dissenter was George.
decoys: All eleven members voted for the decision with no dissents recorded.

points.point: George preferred to signal a near-term tapering of asset purchases
points.quote: Ms. George preferred to signal a near-term tapering of asset purchases, which would begin to move policy toward a more appropriate stance.
paraphrases: George preferred to signal a near-term taper of asset purchases.
George favored an early move toward tapering the Fed's asset purchases.
Esther George wanted the Committee to signal tapering purchases soon.
decoys: George preferred to increase the pace of asset purchases.

points.point: Guidance: highly accommodative policy expected to remain in place at least while unemployment is above 6-1/2 percent and inflation projections are contained
points.quote: this exceptionally low range for the federal funds rate will be appropriate at least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6 1/2 percent
paraphrases: Fed reiterated near-zero rates would stay in place at least until unemployment falls below 6.5%.
Committee kept its 6-1/2% unemployment threshold for considering the first rate hike.
Guidance: rates stay exceptionally low as long as joblessness is above 6.5 percent.
decoys: Committee lowered its unemployment threshold for a hike to 5.5 percent.
Fed said it would hike once unemployment fell below 4 percent.

points.point: Committee signaled willingness to increase or reduce the pace of purchases as the outlook changes

points.quote: The Committee is prepared to increase or reduce the pace of its purchases to maintain appropriate policy accommodation as the outlook for the labor market or inflation changes
paraphrases: Fed signaled it could speed up or slow QE purchases depending on the outlook.
Committee said it stood ready to increase or reduce its buying pace as conditions warrant.
FOMC kept optionality to adjust the pace of asset purchases up or down.
decoys: Committee said the pace of purchases was now fixed and would not change.
Fed committed to ending purchases entirely within two months.

points.point: Inflation running somewhat below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective
points.quote: Inflation has been running somewhat below the Committee's longer-run objective
paraphrases: Inflation ran somewhat below the Fed's 2 percent longer-run objective.
Price gains stayed under the Committee's longer-run 2% goal.
Headline inflation remained below the FOMC's longer-run objective.
decoys: Inflation ran persistently above the Committee's longer-run objective.
Inflation held exactly at the Committee's 2 percent objective, unaffected by energy prices.

points.point: Unemployment rate was 7.6 percent in March
points.quote: The unemployment rate was 7.6 percent in March
paraphrases: Unemployment rate stood at 7.6% in March.
Jobless rate was 7.6 percent last month.
The unemployment rate held at 7.6%, a little below its Q4 average.
decoys: Unemployment rate fell to 6.6 percent in March.
Unemployment rate rose to 8.1 percent in March.

points.point: Fiscal policy (sequestration and tax increases) was seen as restraining economic growth
points.quote: fiscal policy was restraining economic growth
paraphrases: Fiscal tightening (sequestration, tax hikes) was seen as a drag on growth.
Participants said fiscal policy continued to restrain economic activity.
The federal spending sequester was viewed as a headwind to the recovery.
decoys: Fiscal policy was seen as providing a meaningful boost to growth this year.
Participants said monetary policy, not fiscal policy, was the main drag on growth.
